A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same SISL research work, with readable main text and complete Appendices A–G. Text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison of equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v4 reports original SISL experiments across four environments in Section 5 and Table 1, with additional comparisons, robustness tests, and ablations in Appendices D–G.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experimental results in Section 5, Table 1, and Appendices D–G, including benchmark evaluations and component ablations.

M1.justification: The decoupled policies, periodic skill refinement, maximum return relabeling, and buffer mixing remain identical. Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same objectives and algorithms.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Kitchen, Office, Maze2D, and AntMaze with the same task coverage. The limited-data, random-action corruption, suboptimal-data, and explicit-goal scenarios in the appendices are also unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain SAC, SAC+RND, PEARL, PEARL+RND, SPiRL, and SiMPL, plus SAC+HER in Appendix G.6. The newly cited Jo et al. work is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.3 and Appendix C retain identical task splits, data construction, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, and interaction controls. The supplementary experiments also retain their settings.

E4.justification: The component and hyperparameter ablations, data-corruption tests, computational analyses, reward-model checks, and skill/task visualizations in Section 5 and Appendices D–G are unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 in both versions specifies five random seeds and standard deviations shown as shaded graph regions and ± table entries. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All reported values, curves, rankings, and qualitative findings match, including Table 1 and the appendix results. For example, both report SISL Kitchen performance of 3.48±0.07 at noise σ=0.3.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, definitions, and objectives in Sections 3–4 and Appendix B are identical. No assumptions, derivations, formal results, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction’s contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about robust skill refinement, maximum return relabeling, and adaptation from noisy demonstrations. The introductory citation edit does not alter these claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of skill denoising, buffer mixing, reward-model stability, and generalization remain unchanged. Section 6 retains the same computational-overhead and meta-test fine-tuning limitations.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the advertised code address from github.com/epsilog/SISL to epsilog.github.io/SISL. Implementation, hardware, hyperparameter, and data-construction details remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish any change in code availability.

R1.justification: v5 adds Jo et al. (2026), concerning retention of suboptimal actions in multi-agent RL, to the introductory exploration citations. Hwang et al. changes from a 2025 preprint to a 2026 conference reference to the same work. Broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The opening paragraph is lightly rewritten to distinguish exploration improvements from sample-efficiency improvements. Citation metadata and the version/date stamp are updated, while section organization and the remaining narrative are unchanged.

P2.justification: The edits produce limited line reflow on page 1 and bibliography reflow across pages 13–15. All figures, tables, captions, axes, legends, and appendix layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: v5 provides small editorial and bibliographic updates and changes the advertised code address. The method, experimental evidence, technical documentation, and limitations—including all appendices—remain unchanged. These edits do not establish a meaningful overall quality gain or loss, and the PDFs alone cannot establish improved code access.
